summary:
TERRA SIGHT is an interactive satellite intelligence platform designed to make Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Earth observation more accessible. Built around NASA's OPERA RTC-S1 dataset, the platform allows users to explore satellite observations through an interactive 3D Earth interface and discover radar data using geographic and temporal search.

By connecting to NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR), TERRA SIGHT retrieves real satellite observation metadata and presents it in a more approachable geospatial environment. Unlike conventional optical satellite imagery, SAR technology uses radar signals to observe Earth's surface and can collect useful observations regardless of cloud cover or daylight conditions.

Our goal is to reduce the technical barriers to discovering and exploring satellite radar data. TERRA SIGHT demonstrates how NASA's open Earth observation resources can be combined with interactive visualization to support environmental exploration, scientific learning, and a better understanding of our changing planet.
details:
Project Details — TERRA SIGHT

SEE BEYOND THE SURFACE

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

TERRA SIGHT is an interactive satellite-data discovery platform designed to make Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Earth observation more accessible.

The project focuses on NASA's OPERA RTC-S1 dataset, which contains radar observations of Earth's surface. Unlike conventional optical satellite imaging, SAR uses radar signals and can collect observations regardless of daylight and through cloud cover.

Users can explore an interactive 3D representation of Earth, define geographic search areas, specify date ranges, and discover available satellite observations. TERRA SIGHT connects to NASA's Common Metadata Repository (CMR) to retrieve real observation metadata and present the results in a more approachable geospatial interface.

2. What are its benefits?

Satellite radar data can provide valuable information for understanding Earth's surface. However, discovering relevant datasets can be technically challenging.

TERRA SIGHT aims to reduce this barrier by making satellite observation discovery more intuitive.

Potential benefits include:

  • Making NASA satellite data easier to discover.
  • Helping users explore observations by location and date.
  • Supporting environmental research and scientific learning.
  • Making Earth-observation resources more approachable for students, educators, and researchers.

3. What is the intended impact?

Our goal is to make Earth-observation data more accessible.

By connecting NASA's open satellite resources with interactive geospatial visualization, TERRA SIGHT demonstrates how complex scientific datasets can be presented through a more intuitive experience.

The project also introduces users to the value of SAR technology and its role in observing Earth under conditions where conventional optical imagery has limitations.

4. What tools and technologies were used?

Software and programming:

  • JavaScript — application logic and interactive functionality.
  • HTML — interface structure.
  • CSS — visual design and styling.
  • Python — supporting test scripts and automated checks included in the project repository.
  • Three.js — interactive 3D Earth visualization.
  • Vite — frontend development and production builds.
  • Netlify Functions — serverless API functionality.
  • Git and GitHub — version control and source code management.

Scientific data and resources:

  • NASA OPERA RTC-S1 Version 1 — satellite radar observation dataset.
  • NASA Common Metadata Repository (CMR) — satellite observation discovery API.

5. What makes the project creative?

TERRA SIGHT combines satellite-data discovery with an interactive 3D geospatial experience.

Instead of presenting satellite observations only through technical catalogs, the platform gives users a visual starting point for exploring where and when observations are available.

The project brings together Earth science, satellite technology, interactive visualization, and web engineering to make radar-data discovery more approachable.

6. What factors did we consider?

During development, we considered:

  • Scientific accuracy: Connecting to real NASA resources and presenting the project's capabilities accurately.
  • Accessibility: Making satellite-data discovery easier for users without specialized technical knowledge.
  • Data reliability: Using NASA's data services and accounting for possible API and network failures.
  • Technical feasibility: Developing a working prototype within the available competition timeframe.
  • Extensibility: Creating a foundation that could support additional datasets and more advanced analytical capabilities in future versions.

TERRA SIGHT currently focuses on discovering OPERA RTC-S1 observation metadata, with opportunities for future expansion into broader Earth-observation applications.
